ja: 兄が郵便局に間に合ってたら、受け取れたのに。
en: My brother could've gotten it if he'd made it.
alternatives: If he'd made it, my brother could've gotten it.
My brother could've received it if he'd made it.
point: 過去の仮定は had＋過去分詞、結果は could have＋過去分詞

ja: 郵便局の人が小包は明日届くと言ってた。
en: The clerk said the package would arrive tomorrow.
alternatives: The clerk said the parcel would come tomorrow.
The clerk said the package will arrive tomorrow.
point: said の後の that 節は will を would に揃えることが多い

ja: ここに名前を書いてください。
alternatives: Write your name here, please.
Please put your name here.
point: 「書いてください」は Please + 動詞の原形

ja: 市役所は土曜日は休みです。
alternatives: City hall is closed on Saturdays.
City hall isn't open on Saturdays.
point: 毎週のことなので Saturdays と複数形

ja: この申込書、手伝っていただけないかと思いまして。
en: I was wondering if you'd help with this form.
alternatives: Would you mind helping me with this form?
I was hoping you could help me with this form.
Could you possibly help me with this form?
point: 丁寧な依頼は I was wondering if で過去形にして和らげる

ja: 私のカード、もう送りましたか？
en: Have you sent my card yet?
alternatives: Have you mailed my card yet?
Did you already send my card?
point: 疑問文の「もう」は文末の yet で表す

ja: もしキャッシュカードをなくしたら、銀行に電話する？
en: If you lost your card, would you call the bank?
alternatives: Would you call your bank if you lost your card?
If you lost your card, would you call your bank?
point: 仮の話なので if 節は過去形 lost、主節は would you

ja: 母はもう30分も待っています。
en: My mom has waited thirty minutes already.
alternatives: Mom has been waiting for thirty minutes.
My mom's been waiting half an hour.
point: 今も続く待ち時間は現在完了で言う

ja: ATMに長い列ができています。
alternatives: There's a long line at the ATM.
The ATM has a long line.
point: 「列ができている」は There's a long line

ja: 私たちは今、順番を待っています。
alternatives: We're waiting in line now.
We're waiting in line right now.
point: 「順番を待つ」は wait for our turn

ja: 修理の人はスマホは金曜に直ると言ってた。
en: The repairman said it'd be ready Friday.
alternatives: The repairman told me it'd be ready Friday.
The repair guy said it'd be ready Friday.
point: said の後は would で時制を合わせる

ja: このペン、お借りしてもいいですか？
alternatives: Could I borrow your pen?
May I borrow this pen?
point: 「借りる」は borrow、貸すの lend と区別

ja: 終わったら電話してもらえますか？
en: Could you call me when it's done?
alternatives: Can you call me when it's ready?
Would you call me when it's finished?
point: when 節は未来のことでも現在形

ja: なくしたカード、もう再発行してもらった。
en: I've already had my lost card reissued.
alternatives: I already got my lost card reissued.
I've already gotten my lost card reissued.
point: 「〜してもらう」は have + もの + 過去分詞

ja: 修理に出したのは、画面じゃなくてバッテリーですよ。
en: It was the battery I brought in, not the screen.
alternatives: What I brought in was the battery, not the screen.
The battery is what I brought in, not the screen.
point: 強調したい語を It was と that の間に挟む

ja: 窓口の人が、書類の遅れは住所のせいかもと言った。
en: The clerk said my address might delay the documents.
alternatives: The clerk told me my address might delay the documents.
According to the clerk, my address might delay the documents.
point: might を使うと「かも」と断定を避けて伝えられる

ja: 兄は今日、ノートPCを取りに行きます。
en: My brother's picking up his laptop today.
alternatives: My brother will pick up his laptop today.
My brother's going to pick up his laptop.
point: 「取りに行く」は pick up。予定は進行形でも言える

ja: 妹は窓口で、もっと情報が必要だと言われました。
en: My sister was told they needed more information.
alternatives: The clerk told my sister they needed more information.
They told my sister they needed more information.
point: information は数えられない名詞、informations や an は不可
